text: Flare day. Joints on fire, brain fog thick as soup. Cancelled everything. Again. People think I'm flaky; I'm just ill.
Spoon count today: about three. Used two on a shower. Saving the last one for dinner.
Neurologist finally believed me. Seven years of 'it's anxiety' and now there's a name for it. Relieved and furious in equal measure.
Good pain day! Walked to the corner shop and back without the stick. Small things.
Wheelchair access at the theatre was 'temporarily unavailable'. Third time this year. Missed the show Esther got me tickets for.
Feeling okay with my body today, which is rare. It's carrying me through a lot.
Pain clinic appointment moved again. Four months more. I can't plan anything, not even a holiday, around a body like this.
Infusion day. Six hours in the chair. Read a whole book, chatted with Jun in the next chair. Not the worst Tuesday.
Came out to my parents tonight. Mum hugged me. Dad went quiet and then said 'I just want you happy'. I'm shaking with relief.
First Pride. Twenty-nine and finally here. Dancing in the street with strangers who feel like family.
Someone shouted at me and Mattie for holding hands on the bus. Mattie squeezed tighter. I'm still rattled.
Changed my name on the bank account today. Small form, huge feeling. It's really me now.
Hoping the gender clinic writes back soon. Two years on the waiting list. Checking the post every morning.
Lonely being the only queer person in this village. The nearest community group is an hour's bus ride.
Finished the commission for the café mural. Three weeks on scaffolding. Stood back today and felt like it was worth it.
Creative block, day nineteen. Staring at blank canvases. Washed every brush I own twice.
Gallery wants six pieces for the spring show. Six! I've got two finished and a lot of sketches.
Played the piano for two hours without noticing time pass. That's the feeling I chase.
Wondering whether my art is any good or whether I just like making it. Maybe that's enough.
Pottery class: my first bowl that doesn't wobble. Taking it home like a trophy.
Album finished. Sent the masters off. Strange empty feeling now it's out of my hands.
Can't decide between the two job offers and the deadline is Friday. Spreadsheets, lists, sleepless nights.
Dad and I fixed the shed roof. Didn't say much. Good day.
Match on. Pint. Dog asleep on my feet. Sorted.
Lads cancelled the fishing trip. Again. Not bothered. Bit bothered.
Long day on the site. Concrete pour. Knackered but it went in level.
Thinking about what Dad would've made of me now. Reckon he'd be alright with it.
Lambing season. Up four times a night. Lost one ewe, saved her twins. Mixed day.
Hay's in before the rain. Whole family on the trailer. Sat on the bales after with cider.
Milk price dropped again. Feed price up. Not sure how much longer we can keep the herd.
First frost on the fields this morning. Breath clouding, dogs bouncing. Quiet and beautiful.
Market day. Sold all the eggs and most of the honey. Mrs. Fairweather bought six jars for Christmas.
Prayed this morning before the hospital visit. Felt held. Whatever happens, we're not alone in it.
Fasting has made me notice how much I take for granted. Thinking about gratitude all day.
Gurdwara langar today. Served food for four hours with Uncle Harjit. Tired legs, full heart.
Questioning my faith a lot lately. Not losing it, just turning it over in my hands.
Church choir is doing the Messiah at Easter and I've got a solo. Terrified and thrilled.
Too many sounds in the supermarket. Lights buzzing, music, beeping. Left my basket and walked out.
Got my ADHD diagnosis. Thirty-four years of feeling broken and now there's a reason. Spent the evening reading everything.
Hyperfocused on the coding project for nine hours. Forgot lunch. Made something brilliant.
Masked all day at work. Smiled, nodded, small-talked. Home now in the dark with headphones on. So drained.
Found a group for autistic adults that meets on Thursdays. First time I've felt like I'm speaking the same language.
The plan changed at the last minute and my whole day fell apart. I know it's small to others.
Maa made aloo paratha for breakfast and packed extra for office. Feeling very looked after today.
Sharma ji's son got into IIT and now the whole colony is comparing. Not stressed only, just tired of it.
Wedding season again. Three functions this week, mehendi, sangeet, reception. My feet have filed a complaint.
Rishta meeting tomorrow. Mummy has already planned the menu. I have planned my escape. Very nervous.
Board exam results day. 92%. Papa distributed sweets in the whole building before I even saw the marksheet.
Monsoon finally here. Sat on the balcony with chai and pakoras watching the rain. Total peace.
Shifting to Bangalore next month for the new job. Excited, but leaving Nani is breaking my heart.
Auto driver took the long route and charged double. Argued for ten minutes. Lost. Sigh.
Diwali cleaning: every cupboard, every fan, every corner. House is shining. Me, not so much.
Hostel is very quiet this weekend, everyone went home. Me and the mess food.
Dissertation submitted at 11:58pm. Two minutes to spare. I'm free, I'm free, I'm free.
Second year is harder than I thought. Lectures, labs, part-time job, rent. Something has to give.
Seminar went well. I spoke three times and nobody looked at me funny. Small wins.
Library till midnight again. Too tired to walk home. Got a taxi I can't afford.
Graduation in two weeks. Mum and Dad flying in from Nairobi. Already crying thinking about it.
I'm wondering if I picked the wrong course. I love the idea of law more than actually doing it.
Hoping the internship comes through. Final interview went well. They said 'end of the week'.
Flatmates are lovely but loud. Hiding in my room with earplugs just to read a chapter.
Sunday bike ride with Bas along the dyke. Wind in our faces, cheese sandwiches. Good life.
Mum's memory clinic said it's early dementia. Driving home, I kept thinking about all the years we have left and how to fill them.
Visited the grave on his birthday. Told him about the new job. Left a cigar, as a joke he'd have liked.
Six months since Ana died and I laughed properly today. Then felt guilty. Then decided she'd want me to.
Clearing Grandad's shed. Every tin of screws sorted by size. He was so careful. I kept one tin.
Grief group tonight. Seven strangers, one candle, lots of tissues. I wasn't the only one. That helped.
Ordinary day. Walked to the station, worked, came back. Nothing to note.
Worked on the spreadsheet. Sent it to Monique. Lunch at 1.
Car insurance renewed online. Cheaper than last year by a bit.
Planted onions in the raised bed. Watered the tomatoes. Swept the path.
Booked the plumber for next Tuesday. Bought filters for the tap.
Gym at 6, office at 8, home at 6. Pasta. Bed at 11.
Took the cat to the vet for her jabs. All fine. Paid £46.
Returned the parcel at the post office. Got a receipt.
Finished the quarterly report and filed it. Meeting with Lars tomorrow.
It was a day. Some good bits, some bad bits, nothing big either way.
Sorted the bookshelf. Took two bags to the charity shop.
Rang the council about the pothole. Reference number noted.
Thank you to Oskar for lending me his drill and his patience.
Grateful to the night bus driver who waited for me to run the last fifty metres.
My mentor, Dr. Yildiz, read my whole grant proposal on her weekend. I owe her.
Furious that the gym cancelled my membership without telling me and kept charging the card.
Neighbour cut down the tree on my side of the fence without asking. Forty years old. Raging.
The airline cancelled our flight home and offered a voucher. Stranded with two kids. So angry I can't think.
Thinking about how much of my week goes to things I don't care about. Time to cut some.
I wonder if Nadia knows how much that conversation meant. Should tell her.
Midlife audit: good marriage, so-so job, bad knees, great kids. Could be worse. Could be better.
I keep noticing I'm happiest around water. Rivers, sea, even the bath. Something in that.
Excited to start the pottery wheel course on Saturday. Bought an apron already.
New bike arrives tomorrow! Planned my first route along the coast.
Hoping my sister and I can fix things at the wedding. We haven't spoken properly in a year.
The garden is slowly coming back after the flood. New shoots on the roses. Maybe it'll be okay.
Started saving for the deposit properly. £200 a month. Long way to go, but it's a start.
Therapy is slowly helping. I caught myself in the old thought pattern today and stepped out of it.
I think the worst of the money stuff might be behind us. Paid off the last overdue bill today.
Signed up for the evening course in counselling. Maybe this is what I'm meant to do.
Physio says the shoulder's healing well. Swimming again by summer, hopefully.
Missing Ahmed. He moved to Dubai and the evenings feel empty without our chess games.
Third weekend in a row with no plans. Everybody's busy with their families.
Moved to the suburbs for space and now I barely see anyone. Space was overrated.
Even at the party I felt like I was watching through glass. Smiled, left early.
My twin is away for six months on the research ship. I didn't know quiet could be this loud.
Divorce papers signed today. The flat feels enormous and I don't know who to tell.
Feeling completely swamped. Moving house, new team, Gran's operation, all in March.
The wedding planning spreadsheet has 214 rows. I closed it and lay on the floor.
Too much input at the conference. Three days of talks and networking. My brain is full.
Kids sick, deadline moved up, car battery dead, fridge broken. All before 9am.
Every time I tick something off the list two more things appear. Hydra list.
Grandad's 100th birthday party. Telegram from the King, cake the size of a table, and Grandad flirting with the nurse. Perfect.
Bit content today. Garden, sun, a good book.
Satisfying evening repotting every plant in the flat. They look happier. So do I.
Life is simple at the moment and I like it. Work, walks, Sunday calls with my brother.
Dinner with Rahul's family. His aunt kept feeding me. Left full and happy.
Got my first article published in the local paper. Mum bought ten copies.
I've been anxious about the move for weeks, and today it all just worked. Van came, boxes in, keys handed over.
Meditated for twenty minutes without checking the timer. First time.
Quiet evening by the fire. The house is creaking and settling. So am I.
Feeling really sad that Bianca and I fell out over something so small.
Sold Dad's car today. Watched it drive away with someone else at the wheel.
Can't sleep thinking about the job interview tomorrow. Practising answers in the dark.
Exhausted after the move. Every muscle aches and there are still forty boxes.
Drained after the family reunion. Lovely to see everyone. Need a week of silence now.
Long haul flight, then straight into a full workday. Running on airport coffee.
Excited for the first camping trip with the kids. Tent pitched in the garden for practice.
Hopeful that this winter will be gentler than the last. Bought a light box. Booked the coast for February.
